subject: Marketplace procurement path & PO vs Card - LumenAI
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Joe Carter <joe@lumen.ai>, Priya Shah <priya@lumen.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-01T14:30:00Z
Subject: Marketplace procurement path & PO vs Card - LumenAI

Hi Joe & Priya,

Great speaking with you earlier - appreciate the time and the detailed run-through of your infra and procurement constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on the commercial path:

Recap from today's call:
- LumenAI is evaluating Redwood for inference serving across a subset of production ML workloads (recommendation: Dedicated for predictable throughput).
- Main procurement question: Card vs PO for initial engagement; finance typically requires PO for enterprise spend >$10k/mo.
- Marketplace interest: LumenAI asked about AWS Marketplace listing as a way to simplify procurement approvals; also considering GCP/ Azure in longer term.

Open items / asks for procurement readiness:
1) Confirm the procurement contact we should engage for PO process and legal redlines (name + best email).
2) Do you prefer to start via AWS Marketplace (subscription SKU) or a direct Redwood invoice + PO?
3) Any specific compliance docs they need (SOC2, DPA, EU data flow statement)? We can share our standard packet.

Next steps I propose:
- Camila (me) to share a short mutual action plan + two commercial paths (Marketplace vs Direct PO) with estimated timelines.
- If PO: we'll provide a formal quote and PO instructions.
- If Marketplace: I'll share the onboarding checklist and expected listing timeline.

Attaching: redwood_SOW_draft_v1.pdf (SOW draft) and pricing_sheet_q4_2026.xlsx (pricing guidance).

Would love an intro to your procurement lead (if different from Priya) so we can move the paperwork in parallel with technical onboarding.

Thanks - Camila
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0124

-----
Note: Attachment stubs: redwood_SOW_draft_v1.pdf, pricing_sheet_q4_2026.xlsx

From: Joe Carter <joe@lumen.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-02T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Marketplace procurement path & PO vs Card - LumenAI

Thanks Camila - good recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- Procurement policy: for vendor spend >$10k/month we generally require a purchase order. We can use a corporate card for proof-of-concept or small pilot spend under that threshold.
- Marketplace: We're leaning toward AWS Marketplace for ease of approval for our product teams, but finance will need clarity on differences (billing cadence, fees, and who issues invoices).
- Procurement contact: Karen Li (karen.li@lumen.ai) is our procurement lead and will own the PO process. Please loop her in.

Can you provide:
1) Two pricing scenarios (Direct invoice monthly vs AWS Marketplace subscription with marketplace fees included) - line-item estimate so finance can compare.
2) A short PO instructions doc so Karen has what she needs to issue a PO to Redwood.

If you can get those to me by EOD Thursday, I'll route to Karen and finance for a quick review. Thanks - Joe

Joe Carter
Head of Product - LumenAI
joe@lumen.ai | +1 (650) 555-0199

From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Joe Carter <joe@lumen.ai>, Priya Shah <priya@lumen.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-03T10:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Marketplace procurement path & PO vs Card - LumenAI

Appreciate the clarity, Joe - looping in next steps.

Action plan (high level):
- Day 0 (today): Redwood sends two quote documents - (A) Direct invoice monthly quote, (B) AWS Marketplace estimated subscription quote (includes expected 5% marketplace fee markup).
- Day 1-3: Karen / procurement reviews and confirms preferred path.
- If PO path: Karen sends PO to finance@redwood.ai; we'll route to contracts for countersign. Provide PO instructions doc and standard SOW.
- If Marketplace: Redwood starts marketplace onboarding immediately (we'll need technical lead contact for listing and a purchase order is not required for a marketplace subscription but finance still needs SKU/pricing). Marketplace listing typically takes 7-14 business days.

I've attached a marketplace_onboarding_matrix.xlsx that outlines timelines and required artifacts per cloud (AWS/GCP/Azure). I'll also prepare the two formal quote PDFs and a short PO_instructions.pdf.

Quick question for Karen / procurement (when on thread): Is there a preferred PO template or field requirements we should include on the invoice (PO number, contract reference, cost center)? That will help avoid back-and-forth.

Thanks - Camila

From: Priya Shah <priya@lumen.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, Joe Carter <joe@lumen.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karen Li <karen.li@lumen.ai>
Date: 2026-10-05T16:00:00Z
Subject: Re: Marketplace procurement path & PO vs Card - LumenAI

Hi Camila / Joe - looping Karen in as requested.

Karen Li (Procurement) here - thanks for the summary. A few points from procurement:

- For an initial production rollout we prefer AWS Marketplace if it reduces legal/finance friction, but we do need:
  * SKU/pricing information and an example invoice showing how charges will appear.
  * PO instructions that list the exact payee name and address Redwood wants on the PO.
- If we go the PO route, please include your W-9 / tax info and the Redwood legal name for the contract.
- Timeline: procurement review ~1-2 weeks after we have the formal quote and PO instructions.

Next steps for Redwood: please provide the two formal quote PDFs (Direct invoice & Marketplace subscription), a completed PO_instructions.pdf, and any standard compliance docs (SOC2, DPA). If you can attach or link those in reply, we'll start the review.

Thanks - Karen
Karen Li
Procurement Lead | LumenAI
karen.li@lumen.ai

Attachments referenced: PO_instructions.pdf, example_invoice_aws_marketplace.pdf
